title: Interval spelling and inversion
description: Drill letter-first spelling, compound reduction, and the invert-to-9 quality-flip rules.

cards.front: What three skills build on interval names?
cards.back: Spelling (write the correct upper note and letter), compound intervals (9ths, 10ths, and so on vs simple), and inversion (flip the interval by moving one note an octave).

cards.front: What are the two steps for spelling an interval above a lower note?
cards.back: 1) Find the letter: for number n, the upper letter is n − 1 letters above the lower. 2) Choose the accidental so the half-step distance matches the quality.

cards.front: Spell a major 3rd above F♯, showing both steps.
cards.back: Letter two above F is A. F♯ to A is 3 half steps, but a major 3rd is 4, so the note is A♯.

cards.front: Why is a major 3rd above F♯ written A♯, not B♭?
cards.back: Same pitch class, wrong interval. F♯ to B♭ spans F G A B, a 4th, and at that width it is a diminished 4th, not a 3rd.

cards.front: Spell a major 3rd above G♯. Why not write C?
cards.back: B♯. Letters G A B; G♯ to B♯ is 4 half steps. B♯ is C on the guitar, but the spelling is correct in keys such as C♯ major or G♯ minor.

cards.front: What is a compound interval, and how do you simplify it?
cards.back: An interval an octave or more. Subtract an octave to get the simple version and keep its quality. Number: subtract 7 (a 9th is a 2nd, a 13th is a 6th). Half steps: subtract 12.

cards.front: Give the simple form and half steps for M9, m10, M10, P11, P12, and M13.
cards.back: M2 + octave (14), m3 + octave (15), M3 + octave (16), P4 + octave (17), P5 + octave (19), M6 + octave (21).

cards.front: What do simple-interval numbers add to when inverted? List the pairs.
cards.back: They add to 9: 2nd ↔ 7th, 3rd ↔ 6th, 4th ↔ 5th, unison ↔ octave.

cards.front: How do qualities change under inversion?
cards.back: Major ↔ minor, augmented ↔ diminished, perfect stays perfect. Half steps add to 12.

cards.front: Why do inversion numbers sum to 9 and half steps to 12?
cards.back: An interval and its inversion span exactly one octave. If X up to Y uses n letters, Y up to the next X uses 9 − n letters. Wider intervals have narrower complements. Perfect intervals have no major/minor form, so they stay perfect.

cards.front: Can you invert a compound interval directly?
cards.back: No. Reduce it to a simple interval first, then invert.

cards.front: What does each invert to: P5, M3, m3, M2, m2, A4, d7?
Why is the 7th of F♯ major written E♯, not F?
cards.back: Seven-note scales use each letter once. F♯ G♯ A♯ B C♯ D♯ E♯. F is already the root’s letter.

cards.front: C major is C E G. What interval is C up to G, and what is G up to the next C? What stays the same?
cards.back: C to G is a P5. G to C is a P4, the inversion. Pitch classes and chord identity stay the same; only the interval above the lowest note changes.

cards.front: In extended chords, what are the 9th, 11th, and 13th?
cards.back: Simple intervals placed above the octave, same quality: a 9 is a 2nd plus an octave.

cards.front: String 6 fret 2 is F♯. Where is the major 3rd on the same string, and how is it spelled?
cards.back: String 6 fret 6, spelled A♯ (letters F G A), not B♭.

cards.front: C on string 5 fret 3 up to G on string 4 fret 5 is which interval? Invert it on the next strings.
cards.back: A P5. G on string 4 fret 5 up to C on string 3 fret 5 is a P4. Same two pitch classes, inverted.

cards.front: What interval is C3 on string 5 fret 3 up to D4 on string 2 fret 3?
cards.back: A major 9th: 14 half steps, which is a M2 plus an octave.

cards.front: Spell a major 3rd above A, E♭, F♯, B♭, and D♭.
cards.back: C♯, G, A♯, D, F.

cards.front: Spell a perfect 5th above B, F♯, E♭, D♭, and F.
Spell a minor 3rd above C♯, B♭, E, and F. Then a minor 7th above G and a major 7th above F.
cards.back: E, D♭, G, A♭. Then F and E.

cards.front: Invert each: M3, P4, m7, A4, d7.
Find a major 3rd above open string 3 (G3) in two places. Why are they the same pitch?
cards.back: String 3 fret 4, and open string 2 (B3). Between strings 3 and 2 the same fret is already a major 3rd.
